The entire experience was a 10 out of 10. I recently went here for my birthday and let me tell you food is an art and the chef was an artist who takes their craft seriously. Every dish had amazing flavor and had me truly appreciating the perfect flavor components. I got the raw oysters as a side order that had a perfectly balanced brine of ocean and savory taste that takes your taste buds on an amazing ride containing Fresno Chili Escabeche Mignonette,

It was buttery perfection that melts in your mouth leaving you want to savor every taste with a sauce,garlic, and vegetable filled garnish that was worth every cent. For dessert I had strawberries and cream which includes Chiffon Cake, Crème Fraîche, Raspberry, Sesame Crumble, Vanilla-Rose Ice Cream, Citrus Po with very ripe and flavorful berries and I left feeling extremely satisfied and full. Something you should experience at least once and you'll definitely want to come back for more

text.text:
My partner and I had a reservation for this restaurant and as soon as we walked in, we were greeted with the smell of desserts and snacks. The style of the restaurant is immaculate as there's a golden/white sparkling when entering, similar to marble type environment, super modern and well designed.

Parking is a bit limited, no designated structure or lot but plenty of paid parking lots across/nearby to accommodate, not too expensive.

Since we had a reservation, we were seated super quick even though it was quite busy. Service was great, our server checked up on us on our order and refills very often along with ordering speed.
We ordered a margarita pizza, omelette, and a "must try" Portobello Fries, all shareable dishes. Pizza was bigger than expected but it was super delicious with a nice crunchy crust. Omelette is well cooked and has good portions.

Although I feel like there was too much veggies and less of the omelette, nonetheless, still pretty yummy. Lastly, the Portobello Fries were an absolute treat, as someone who loves mushrooms and fries, this was a perfect combo.

Highly recommend even for non mushroom lovers. Only downside to the fries is the container that it comes in, although great aesthetic, the pieces that fall off can easily make a mess on the table, not a huge downside but one to look at.

After the meal, we took a look at the bakery and we were enamored with the amount of macaron choices, a huge variety and super affordable. There were plenty of other desserts but we were too full to continue! We will definitely be back to try other menu items and bakery catalogs. Food was amazing, dessert is plentiful, service is great, and environment is perfect for a date setting.

text.text:
This was our first time dining here, and it had been on our to-do list for quite some time, especially knowing that an Iron Chef is the owner. My wife and I met up with another couple for dinner and were excited to finally give it a try.

The space offers a vibrant and energetic atmosphere. The décor is nice simple, clean, filled with tasteful greenery, and thoughtfully spaced to create a comfortable dining experience.

We worked our way through the menu and ordered seven items along with cocktails: naan & dips, pickled pepper blueberry cornbread, sautéed green beans, wood-fired broccoli, goat shank, sticky glazed pork shank, and grilled kalbi-style short ribs.

The one dish we were most excited about was the goat curry, but we were told it wasn't available. While waiting for our food, a runner brought a bowl of goat curry to our table, only for us to find out it was meant for another table. Naturally, we asked our server what was going on, and he explained that the other guests had ordered it earlier. In reality, the restaurant had simply sold out. Our reservation was at 6:30 p.m., and the restaurant opens at 5:00 p.m., so it was surprising that such a popular menu item was already gone.

As for the food, everything was cooked very well and beautifully presented. The proteins were moist and tender, and the vegetables were cooked perfectly. The cornbread and naan were excellent standouts. While the proteins were certainly good, the flavors didn't quite reach that "chef's kiss" level for me. They were enjoyable but left me wanting a bit more depth and flavor. The Pork Shank was the better of the proteins.

Service, unfortunately, was the weakest part of the evening. Our server, David, seemed to lack attention to detail. He never offered clean plates as we shared multiple dishes, nor did he check in to see if we wanted additional cocktails or more food. It felt like several missed opportunities to enhance both our  experience and restaurants sales opportunity. Whether he was overwhelmed, distracted, or simply disengaged, the service came across as mediocre.

Overall, the restaurant has great potential. The atmosphere is inviting, the food is well executed.  With more consistent service and better communication regarding menu availability, the experience could easily be elevated.

text.text: An overall good dining experience for the ambience and people watching. I recommend the outdoor seating since the inside can be noisy. The food was all over the place and felt like it was trying too hard, reminiscent of when nouveau CA cuisine was starting. The naan and hummus was a blend of non complimentary flavors thrown together. The naan, heavily garlic seasoned did not pair well with the soy and carrot hummus. The top layer of the naan was delicious and the bottom layer was good with the sides but together with flavors negating each other. Less is more and pick a lane. The pork shank was good and probably the best dish we had with flavors very similar to a pastor taco…if that is the direction and comparison the kitchen wants to evoke then it’s a poor comparison for food that is different and slightly more elevated than the flavors of the LA pastor street taco for a much lower price point. The goat curry was muted and lackluster and was very similar to a chilaquiles with the fried naan chips. Are the slightly better flavors, presentation, and ambiance justifying the significant higher price point? The sad answer is no. There is a heaviness and sweetness to the food which made us feeling still hungry with leftovers. It lacked a savory filling element since the sweetness from the pork and the coconut in the curry negated and fullness from the meats. The accompanying pickled veggies in all three dishes with their bright acidity helped cut through the sweetness and heavy “bready” feeling in all of the dishes. Especially in the competitive LA restaurant scene where even the mom and pop hole in the walls are far better than even Bib Gourmand Michelin restaurants this place pales in comparison. It’s pretty and pleasant but lacking. The goat curry was better the next day as leftovers than at the restaurant.

Came here around 5pm and got seated right away, but by the time we left there was a line. Definitely recommend coming early ⏰

First off, the vibe. Outdoor seating with this slightly European feel, which I honestly did not expect in Downtown LA 🇮🇹✨ It just felt really nice and relaxed.

Food came out super fast, which we appreciated.
We got the calamari in zimino and the meatballs, and both were great — but also really good value.
The calamari portion was generous (lots of squid 🦑), and the meatballs came in a solid portion too, like around 8 pieces. Not small at all.

The house salad was kind of a last-minute order because we saw it at the next table and it looked so good… and yeah, no regrets 🥗 Really fresh, nice mix of veggies, just very well put together.

For mains, I got the gnocchi and my partner got the frutti di mare pasta 🍝 The flavors were honestly so good. Rich, well-balanced, and just satisfying.

I have to say — the seafood pasta was loaded. If you have eaten around LA, you know how rare that is 😭 They were not holding back at all, especially for the price.

As for the gnocchi, it was more on the softer side rather than super chewy, but it worked really well with the mushroom ragu. Paired it with house wine and it just made sense 🍷 Finished the whole plate without even realizing.

Dessert was the cannoli, and wow… crispy shell, super creamy filling, not too sweet. I almost ordered another one 🥲

Overall, great vibe, great food, and really good prices. Definitely adding this to my “come back and run it again” list 💯

text.text:
Redbird delivered one of those rare group dining experiences where everything actually works, even with a party of 13. We came here for a birthday, and from the moment you walk into that stunning former cathedral space, it feels elevated but still warm and inviting. The lighting, the architecture, the energy, it all sets the tone for something special without feeling overly formal.

Chef Neal Fraser’s menu is thoughtful and really well executed, and we went deep into it. The hamachi crudo was my favorite, bright, citrusy, with that perfect sweet and sour balance and just enough crunch to make every bite interesting. The branzino was a standout, clean, delicate, and beautifully cooked. The burrata was another highlight, served over arugula with a balsamic glaze and nuts that added the right amount of texture. Even the brussels sprouts surprised us, a little kick to them and full of flavor. The steak frites were solid, and the fries across the board were fresh, crisp, and addictive.

Dessert sealed it. The pavlova, which I don’t usually gravitate toward, was incredible, light, balanced, and the grapefruit brought a brightness that made it memorable. The s’mores dessert was also a hit, fun, indulgent, and done really well.

Service and pacing, especially for a group this size, were seamless. Everyone felt taken care of, dishes came out smoothly, and the entire experience felt intentional from start to finish. Overall, food, service, and ambience were all excellent.

More on social media: @ratedbymaryam

Oh dear Redbird. My expectation for this restaurant was pretty high as I heard great things. I’ve been trying to try Redbird since Father’s Day 2025. Just a back story on that, I made a reservation for June 15 2025, I received an email from the floor manager telling me all reservations have been canceled due to an event. Mind you, I get this email on June 13th. I was annoyed because I had to scramble and find a restaurant that had availability. I’m sure they knew of this event a while ago. So that was annoying. In September of 2025, I reached out to the floor manager, Ani, and tried to make a reservation for September 14th. She informed me that they will be closed for an event. So I reached out to Ani one last time to get a reservation for my anniversary on April 21st. We finally got in!

So with all of the back and forth with Ani, I kind of expected them to go above and beyond. But unfortunately, I felt we were treated not so great. When we arrived, we waited a good 10 mins until the hostess greeted us. The time we were there, no one acknowledged our presence. When she finally came, she did apologized and walked us over to a big table in the farthest corner in the restaurant. Now mind you, it was only 3 of us, and they tried to sit us at a table that can seat 6, in a corner. No no, I’m not sitting there. I’ve literally been trying to come here for the past 9months and it’s my anniversary. So I asked to be sat at a smaller table in the middle of the restaurant. Now, I’m familiar on how the seating works as it really comes down to the amount of servers  you have and the amount of tables are within their section. But again, the manager Ani, was fully aware of my reservation and I felt that she should’ve provided better hospitality for us.

So, once we were seated, we waited awhile for our waiter. When he finally showed up, we placed our order. We had drinks, appetizers, and our main meal. The menu is on the smaller side, so I expected the food to be overly delicious. But it was just ok. It was good, but not mind blowing. After dinner, I asked the waiter if I can speak with Ani. She came and I reminded her who I was and the back and forth emails we’ve had since July 2025. She knew right away. I told her I was a bit disappointed that the hostess was trying to sit us in the far corner. All she said was “oh sorry about that”. That was it, no complementary dessert, or anything. Like wow! We’ve been treated so much better at other restaurants. It was real disappointing. I would not recommend this spot nor would I come back. I suggest the managers do more hospitality trainings.

Be warned that the pricing is exorbitant across the board—charging $3.75 for a single Long Island clam is absurd. I might return for a beer at the bar, but this spot feels geared much more toward business travelers on expense accounts rather than everyday locals.

I recently stopped by Grand Central Market and it’s one of those places that just feels alive the second you walk in. The energy is hard to miss—busy, loud, and full of people from all walks of life grabbing a bite. It’s not fancy, but that’s exactly the appeal.

What I like most is the variety. You’ve got everything from tacos and BBQ to ramen and fresh pastries all under one roof. It’s perfect if you’re with a group and everyone wants something different. I tried a couple different vendors, and everything was fresh and packed with flavor. You can tell a lot of these spots take pride in what they’re serving.
Seating can be a bit of a challenge, especially during peak hours, so don’t expect a quiet, relaxed meal. It’s more of a grab-your-food-and-find-a-spot kind of place. But honestly, that’s part of the experience. It feels authentic and unpolished in a good way.

Prices are reasonable considering the quality and the location in downtown L.A. It’s also a great place to just wander, try something new, and maybe step outside your comfort zone a bit.

Overall, I’d definitely go back. It’s not about a single restaurant—it’s about the whole experience. If you enjoy food halls with character and great variety, this place is worth the visit.

text.text:
I was visiting my good friend in LA, and we wanted to try this spot as it is quite the popular sushi place known to locals (apparently). My friend’s coworkers had also highly recommended it, so we had high hopes checking it out.

We came in around 5pm, and there was no wait. The restaurant was full, but it was slightly before the dinner rush so we had no trouble getting seated.
The biggest problem was the service.
We were handed about 4 different menus, and since it was our first time here, we tried flagging our server down to ask about the menu and the differences. Myself included, most of my party had either worked in sushi restaurants or had sushi in Japan multiple times (we are all korean) and was expecting a more Japanese sushi experience rather than an Americanized version, so we wanted to ask for specifics like if they had Hitsumabushi or specific cuts of fish we could order. There was also some vagueness  with the menu as the nigiri ordering form lacked prices.

Whenever we tried to flag our server down, she was very dismissive and acted like we were bothering her. She would walk away before we had a chance to ask her additional questions, and would answer very rudely- it ended up taking over 30 minutes just to try to order, as she kept walking past us when we kept flagging her down. She was Japanese, and we were a bit taken aback as every Japanese establishment we’ve visited always prided in excellent service. We wanted to order the Sashimi Deluxe and asked her what fish comes in the deluxe, and she said “Salmon. tuna.” and walked away. We ended up asking for a different server because there was no way for us to enjoy our meal with her as our server.
Our new server was extremely sweet and apologetic about our experience.

As for the food-
Some of the plates smelled like the dishwasher/ mildew, which caused the fish to smell a little off. Here are the things we ordered:

-unagi dinner: for it being more than $30, this was a small portion and the rice smelled weird. We expected larger portioned sides but the sides were small.
-Sashimi deluxe: it was plated very pretty and was decent, but wasn’t as high quality as we had hoped.
-Nigiri: the salmon belly was decent, the regular salmon was a little smelly. The tamago was a big portion and decent, and we enjoyed the yellowtail as well. We were open to ordering more initially, but after seeing the quality, we didn’t move forward with additional orders.

We wanted to potentially order drinks but the first server snatched it away before we got a chance. We ended up just ordering hot tea and water. We also wanted to keep the menu to potentially order more later, but she took it away as well. We came planning on ordering a lot and tipping accordingly, but it seems like she didn’t want us to order a lot of food.

Overall, the fish quality was so-so, it wasn’t mind blowing enough to warrant driving out to LA for, as I feel that plenty of Orange County sushi restaurants can offer a similar quality. For the food I’d say the quality was a 2.5-3/5, however it was our initial encounter with the server that left a bad taste in our mouths. We really appreciated our male server (F or J name) and other female japanese server (Saki?) for improving our experience, but the initial animosity from the first server was so large that we did not want to return. We noticed the other tables in that server’s section also having a bad time with her service, as we saw her and the guests having some unhappy interactions. I don’t think it was racism, perhaps the server was having a bad day. But even if the service is subpar, we would have been okay if we were at least served quickly and efficiently, but that did not happen with her either, hence us requesting a new server.

Interior was cute, did not try the bathroom. Noise level was quite loud, and pretty busy once the dinner rush picked up.

Parking has a fee and is sparse. I’d say try to come before 5pm if you want to park and get in without too long of a wait.

Had dinner here with two friends on July 6th, 2025. The space has a warm and rustic-industrial vibe, fitting for a modern Italian restaurant that’s earned its Michelin nod. The service was attentive without being intrusive, and the staff gave helpful recommendations throughout the evening.

We started with the brodetto, a comforting bowl of steamed clams and mussels served with toasted crostini. The seafood was fresh and flavorful, and the broth had a savory depth that paired nicely with the crispy bread. A great way to begin the meal.

For pasta, we tried the mandilli, which were vibrant green, handkerchief-like sheets of pasta with a delicate, buttery sauce. The texture was silky and smooth—simple but elegant. The pappardelle with slow-braised pork was rich and satisfying, with wide ribbons of pasta soaking up the meaty, aromatic sauce.

We also shared one of their ligurian focaccinas—the funghi—which came with melted cheese, wild mushrooms, and fresh herbs on a thin, crisp pastry base. The crust was light and flaky, and the mushrooms added an earthy contrast to the richness of the cheese.

While the meal was overall delicious and thoughtfully prepared, we found that some dishes were a touch too salty, especially the pork pappardelle. It didn’t ruin the experience, but it’s worth noting for those sensitive to seasoning.

Portions were fair, and the pricing reflected the quality and presentation. All in all, this is a great spot for upscale Italian fare with bold flavors and creative execution. We’d gladly return, perhaps to try more from the seafood and vegetable sections of the menu.

My husband and I dined at Rossoblu and loved the food, space, and hospitality so much that we ended up having our wedding reception here. We’re so glad we did.

They very accommodating from the start, even setting up an impromptu tasting so we could sample the menu. So many dishes were excellent especially the stracciatella and winter citrus, tuna crudo (the pistachio caper sauce is delicious), rosemary focaccia with mortadella mousse, hanger steak, and apennine fries (never had fries like this). Our favorite pastas were the tagliatelle and lasagna bianco (both perfectly cooked texture) and favorite cocktail was the vesuvio. We had a stacked wedding menu that our guests raved about, not just for a wedding but also as a restaurant. There was so much food that servers packed leftovers for guests to bring home. The bar was also very generous with the drinks and even remembered people's orders.

Everyone from the servers, host, bartenders, coordinator, and manager were so hospitable and kind from our first visit. They added to the fun during our wedding and now treat us like family. The service was fast during the night, and the team was also easy to work with throughout planning.

The outdoor and indoor space are beautiful with an industrial chic vibe. We were drawn to the high ceilings, hanging lights, open space, and large windows.

We’re glad we can always return to dine here (as we already have). We highly recommend Rossoblu whether for a meal or a full event.

Someone recommended this restaurant after seeing it on Instagram. I was skeptical from the start because many social media videos are basically promotions. But let me share my direct and honest experience.

Last week, on a weekday afternoon, my family and I were nearby and hungry, so we decided to give it a try. The place immediately felt clumsy, with odd, mismatched décor & not at all what you’d expect from a “fancy” restaurant. We were greeted with the coldest smile and shown to a table. The server looked disheveled, uninterested, and acted like he hadn’t showered in ages. From the beginning, he seemed totally disengaged.

When he brought water glasses, he banged them on the table, and when he served plates, he literally threw them down in a way you wouldn’t even treat someone in jail. That set the tone.

We ordered samosas first, but they were terrible: just bland potato and peas stuffed inside, neither fried nor baked properly. Easily one of the worst samosas I’ve had. The sev puri was just okay. Then came the entrées Butter Chicken and Chicken Tikka Masala. Both dishes were drowning in cream yet completely lacking in flavor. text.text:
Bestia is a must-visit every time I’m in Los Angeles. It’s one of my favorite Italian restaurants, and the quality has been consistently outstanding on every visit.

The food is always creative, flavorful, and beautifully executed. Their wood-fired pizzas are incredibly thin and perfectly crisp. My favorite dish is the bone marrow appetizer—it’s something I order almost every time. They also have a strong wine list, which is great if you enjoy pairing wine with your meal.

One thing I appreciate is that when ordering wine by the glass, the sommelier is willing to bring one or two samples for guests to taste before deciding. However, I wish there had been a little more explanation behind the recommendations. Since we were ordering glass by glass and pairing wines with different dishes, it would have been helpful to hear why those specific wines were suggested and how they would complement the food we ordered. For guests like me who enjoy learning about food and wine pairing but are not wine professionals, that extra guidance would make the experience even better.

The pacing of the food service can be a little slow at times, but it’s still acceptable and doesn’t take away from the overall experience.

Overall, Bestia continues to be one of my favorite restaurants in LA, and I highly recommend it. Be sure to make reservations well in advance—about two weeks ahead for a small group, and at least three weeks ahead for larger parties if you’re hoping to dine during prime dinner hours around 6:00–7:00 PM.

If you plan to dine here, extremely cautious when ordering wine from the sommelier！！ Food at Bestia is undeniably good, but their wine presentation and customer service leave a lot to be desired.

During our visit, the wines were displayed in a line ( picture 1) .  We started with a first bottle priced around $60+.( picture 2 ) When it came time for a second bottle, the restaurant was incredibly noisy. We asked for the white Burgundy he showed to us and then he verbally mentioned the price—however, he spoke so softly in the loud environment that it was almost impossible to hear. Crucially, the sommelier never handed us a physical wine menu to verify the price.
When the bill arrived, we were shocked to find that the second bottle (a white Burgundy) was charged at $650. While Burgundy can be expensive, this mark-up is beyond reason—online retail for the exact bottle is around €280, yet Bestia marks it up to $650.

When we emailed Bestia privately after returning home—simply suggesting that they improve their process by showing guests a physical menu, especially in such a noisy setting—their response was condescending and dismissive. They took zero responsibility, brushed it off entirely, and blamed us for "not checking the menu."

When a sommelier is guiding your selection, it’s natural to rely on their recommendation rather than demanding a physical book that wasn’t even offered. Judging by how rehearsed and indifferent their customer support was, this feels like a well-practiced tactic to push high-margin bottles onto unsuspecting guests in a loud room.

A 20% tip should reflect exceptional service. That wasn’t the experience I had.

The lack of transparency left a bad impression and felt dishonest. With so many great restaurants in Los Angeles that offer better food, better service, and straightforward billing, I wouldn’t recommend this place.

The star of the show was the cheeseburger, but it wasn’t necessarily anything to write home about. It tasted good, the beef was seasoned, and the toppings were fresh. The prices were reasonable for DTLA and a hotel restaurant, but still a bit high for the delivery.

There are better places to spend $25+ per person on a better tasting meal, but I wouldn’t say this place is terrible or anything—it’s a middle-of-the-road spot with OK food, but not much more.
